2023_028_m061323bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting held June 13, 2023 in the Media Center at Troy High School, 4777 Northfield Parkway, called to order by President Schmidt at 7:30 p.m. and adjourned at 8:31 p.m. The Board held the public hearing on the 2023/2024 proposed budget, appointed Kristin Crowe as Special Education Supervisor on a two-year probationary administrative contract effective July 1, 2023, and approved an eight-item consent agenda. Its largest financial action was awarding a voice communication system to Forerunner Technologies for $591,484.49 from the 2023 Capital Projects Fund; a second award sent bid pack 38 for doors and window replacement to Daniels Glass Inc. for $457,297.00.
2023_028_m061323bdmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Troy Board of Education regular meeting, June 13, 2023, held in the Media Center at Troy High School, 4777 Northfield Parkway. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:30 p.m. and it adjourned at 8:31 p.m. Minutes signed by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education (typist notation GH/jh).

**Attendance**
Present with Mr. Schmidt were Board members Alic, Anne, Haupt, and Wilson. Mr. Hauff and Dr. Philippart were absent. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Keyser, Foren, Young, Cross, Pagel, and West. Approximately 20 members of the audience attended.

**Recognition — TSD Mission Moment: Baker Student Civilian Award**
The Board recognized Baker 7th grade student David Kalaj for bravery in saving the life of a person who was drowning at the bottom of a pool the previous summer; the person was revived after receiving CPR. The Troy Police Department awarded David a Civilian Citation on May 18th at the Police Memorial Day celebration. Baker Principal Jonathan Cross introduced the student, who received a certificate of recognition.

**Personnel — Resolution 23-044**
Mr. Schmidt changed the order of the agenda to move Personnel up and invited Mr. Pagel to present. Moved by Dr. Wilson, supported by Mrs. Anne: a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure issued to Ms. Kristin Crowe as Special Education Supervisor, Services Building, effective July 1, 2023. Yes 5, No 0, Absent Hauff and Philippart. A brief recess followed.

**Public Hearing — 2023/2024 Proposed Budget**
Mr. West presented the proposed budget with a PowerPoint, covering tax values, homestead/non-homestead millage, general fund adjustments and assumptions, ancillary funds, the sinking fund and capital projects fund, student enrollment, foundation allowance history, and revenues and expenditures. The Board indicated it had reviewed the proposed budget in its entirety at the June 6th Workshop. There were no additions and deletions and no public communication on agenda items.

**General — Consent Agenda, Resolution 23-045**
Moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Mrs. Alic, to approve items A through H. Yes 5, No 0, Absent Hauff and Philippart.

| Item | Description |
| --- | --- |
| A | Minutes of the May 2, 2023 Special Board of Education Meeting |
| B | Minutes of the May 2, 2023 Closed Session Meeting |
| C | Minutes of the May 2, 2023 Board of Education Workshop |
| D | Minutes of the May 2, 2023 Board of Education Meeting |
| E | Treasurer's Report — April 2023 |
| F | Vehicle Purchase |
| G | 2022/2023 Budget Amendment |
| H | 2023/2024 Budget Appropriations Resolution |

**Curriculum**
None.

**Business — Awards**

| Resolution | Item | Vendor | Amount | Funding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 23-046 | Voice Communication System | Forerunner Technologies | $591,484.49 | 2023 Capital Projects Fund |
| 23-047 | Bid pack 38 — Bemis, Hill, Schroeder, AHS & THS Doors/Window Replacement | Daniels Glass Inc. | $457,297.00 | Capital Projects Fund and/or Building Site and Sinking Fund |

Resolution 23-046 was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mr. Haupt; 23-047 was moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Dr. Wilson. Both passed Yes 5, No 0, with Hauff and Philippart absent.

**Public Communication (Non-Agenda Items)**
Mr. Matt Sackrison, TSD parent, spoke on the District's Robotics program and suggested seeking a coordinator, especially at the elementary levels. Mrs. Katie MacFarland, TSD parent, spoke about pornographic books in District media centers and donated the book How Pornography Harms to the Board. Mr. Alex Karpowitsch, TSD parent, asked to see the data guiding the District's curriculum change. Mr. Jeff Schaeper, a TSD resident with graduates from Troy Schools, said the curriculum change design process did not include parents as stakeholders and provided a slide from the accountability presentation as an example.

**Other and Board Member Comments**
Other: none. Mr. Haupt congratulated graduates and all students; Mrs. Anne and Dr. Wilson shared the same sentiment. Dr. Machesky announced the TFEE Golf Outing on June 20th at Greystone Golf Club, a fundraiser providing grants for teachers; noted only half days remained and that IA-East's last day would be June 20th; and said work continues on the Athens principal position with a special meeting likely before the end of the month. Mr. Schmidt said the Section 1 application for the Natural Resource Trust Fund would be held the following morning at 9:15 a.m. and that he would attend, and announced the next Board meeting for Tuesday, July 18th at the Administration Building at 9:30 a.m., adding that summer Board meetings are not recorded.
2023_028_m061323bdmtg.verbose:
Official minutes of the regular meeting of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held June 13, 2023 at Troy High School, 4777 Northfield Parkway, specifically in the school's Media Center. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:30 p.m. The minutes are respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, and carry the typist notation GH/jh.

ATTENDANCE. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, Board members Alic, Anne, Haupt, and Wilson were present. Mr. Hauff and Dr. Philippart were absent. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Keyser, Foren, Young, Cross, Pagel, and West. Approximately 20 members of the audience attended.

RECOGNITION — TSD MISSION MOMENT: BAKER STUDENT CIVILIAN AWARD. The Board recognized David Kalaj, a Baker 7th grade student, for his bravery in saving the life of a person who was drowning at the bottom of a pool the previous summer. Thanks to David's quick response, the person was revived after receiving CPR. The Troy Police Department awarded David a Civilian Citation on May 18th at the Police Memorial Day celebration. Baker Principal Jonathan Cross was invited up to introduce the student and share more about his story. David received congratulations from the Board along with a certificate of recognition.

PERSONNEL — ADMINISTRATIVE APPOINTMENT, SPECIAL EDUCATION SUPERVISOR (CROWE), RESOLUTION 23-044. Mr. Schmidt changed the order of the agenda and moved Personnel up, inviting Mr. Pagel to present the administrative positions brought to the Board for consideration. It was moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Mrs. Anne that BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED that the Board of Education issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Ms. Kristin Crowe, who will begin her duties as Special Education Supervisor, Services Building, effective July 1, 2023. The vote was Yes 5, No 0, with Hauff and Philippart recorded absent. A brief recess followed.

BUSINESS — PUBLIC HEARING, 2023/2024 PROPOSED BUDGET. Mr. West presented the details of the proposed budget to the Board and community and shared a PowerPoint presentation. He noted the proposed budget had been reviewed in great detail with the Board at the June workshop. His presentation addressed tax values, homestead and non-homestead millage, and general fund adjustments and assumptions. He spoke about ancillary funds, the sinking fund, and the capital projects fund, among others. He also reviewed student enrollment, the District's foundation allowance history, and revenues and expenditures. The Board indicated that it had reviewed the proposed budget in its entirety at the June 6th Workshop.

ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS. None.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (AGENDA ITEMS). None.

GENERAL — CONSENT AGENDA, RESOLUTION 23-045. It was moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Alic that BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED that the Troy Board of Education takes action to approve items A, B, C, D, E, F, G, and H on the consent agenda. The items were: minutes of the May 2, 2023 Special Board of Education Meeting; minutes of the May 2, 2023 Closed Session Meeting; minutes of the May 2, 2023 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the May 2, 2023 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report — April 2023; Vehicle Purchase; 2022/2023 Budget Amendment; and 2023/2024 Budget Appropriations Resolution. The vote was Yes 5, No 0, with Hauff and Philippart absent.

CURRICULUM. None.

BUSINESS — VOICE COMMUNICATION SYSTEM, RESOLUTION 23-046. It was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mr. Haupt that BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED that the purchase of a voice communication system be awarded to Forerunner Technologies in the amount of $591,484.49, and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. The vote was Yes 5, No 0, with Hauff and Philippart absent.

BUSINESS — BEMIS, HILL, SCHROEDER, AHS & THS DOORS/WINDOW REPLACEMENT, RESOLUTION 23-047. It was moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Dr. Wilson that BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED that the bid for bid pack 38 be awarded as follows to Daniels Glass Inc. in the amount of $457,297.00 and that this be approved as an expenditure of the Capital Projects Fund and/or Building Site and Sinking Fund. The vote was Yes 5, No 0, with Hauff and Philippart absent. The agenda heading identifies the affected buildings as Bemis, Hill, and Schroeder elementary schools together with Athens High School (AHS) and Troy High School (THS).

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (NON-AGENDA ITEMS). Four speakers addressed the Board. Mr. Matt Sackrison, a TSD parent, spoke about the District's Robotics program and suggested seeking a coordinator to support the program, especially at the elementary levels. Mrs. Katie MacFarland, a TSD parent, addressed the Board about pornographic books in the District's media centers and gave the Board a book as a donation, How Pornography Harms. Mr. Alex Karpowitsch, a TSD parent, addressed the Board about the change in curriculum and asked to see the data that guided the District's decision to adopt the change. Mr. Jeff Schaeper, a TSD resident with graduates from Troy Schools, addressed the Board about the curriculum change design process and stated that it did not include parents, who are the stakeholders; he provided a slide from the accountability presentation as an example.

OTHER. None.

BOARD MEMBER COMMENTS. Mr. Haupt congratulated all the graduates and all students for completing another school year. Mrs. Anne and Dr. Wilson shared the same sentiment. Dr. Machesky announced that the TFEE Golf Outing would be held on June 20th at Greystone Golf Club and that the fundraiser would provide grants for teachers, putting money back into the classroom. He shared that only half days remained in the school year and that IA-East would have its last day on June 20th. He also reported that the District was working to punctuate the Athens principal position and would likely hold a special meeting before the end of the month to approve it. Mr. Schmidt shared that the Section 1 application for the Natural Resource Trust Fund would be held the following morning at 9:15 a.m. and that he would be in attendance. He announced that the next Board meeting would be held on Tuesday, July 18th at the Administration Building at 9:30 a.m., and added that summer Board meetings are not recorded.

ADJOURNMENT. The meeting adjourned at 8:31 p.m.
